chapter_name: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the hidden chemistry of everyday things by classifying them into acids, bases, and neutral substances using magical color-changing indicators!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Have you ever wondered why lemons taste so sour and soap feels so slippery? Acids are substances that usually taste sour, like vinegar or curd. Bases are the opposite, they taste bitter and feel soapy to the touch!

Since we cannot taste every chemical to check what it is, scientists use special substances called indicators. These are like chemical spies that change their color completely to reveal if a substance is an acid or a base.

What happens when an acid and a base meet? They battle it out and cancel each other's effects! This process creates a brand new neutral substance called salt and water, which is neither acidic nor basic.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 DIY Turmeric Magic Paper
fun_activity.instructions: Mix some turmeric powder with water to make a paste and rub it on a paper. Once it dries, use a cotton swab dipped in soapy water to draw on it and watch the yellow paper magically turn red because soap is a base!

quick_recap: ⭐ Acids are sour, and bases are bitter and soapy.
⭐ Indicators like turmeric and litmus paper change color to tell us if something is acidic or basic.
⭐ Mixing an acid and a base neutralizes them, forming salt and water.
